correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the C_M multiplier is (Z+1)^2/Z on K[Z]/((Z+1)^M), so its j-th kernel has dimension min(2j,M) and it has two zero blocks of size h=M/2. For each twice-odd cycle the local dimension is two; the root 1 has zero multiplier and a nontrivial root gives one size-two block because the derivative is nonzero. A transverse resonance has η=ζ or ζ^{-1}, so there are the identity pair and 2(g−1) nontrivial ordered pairs. The identity gives four J_1 blocks, the others each two J_2 blocks under the square-zero sum. For h a power of two with h≥2, J_h⊞J_2 is two J_h blocks since K[U,V]/(U^h,V²)=K[U+V,V]/((U+V)^h,V²). Nonzero transverse eigenvalues cannot become zero by a sum with a nilpotent longitudinal operator. This yields exactly 16g−8 blocks of size h, not a generalized nullspace of dimension 16g−8. The off-diagonal block form gives rank B=(N−dim ker A)/2 and character orthogonality makes the positive reduced-state eigenvalues equal to 2^{−rank B}. The two equal-volume examples evaluate as claimed. An independent physical-adjacency GF(2) check agreed for (4,6,6), (4,6,10), (8,6,6), and (4,10,10), including all power ranks through h+1, without executing supplied scripts; replay: /workspace/branches/7a6309c0-ea6d-4bfe-8b18-7f8e5c4751e8/record5_independent.py. Those checks are finite, not the proof.
